markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small SASRec extension with independently measurable components. No validation gains are established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already represents ordered context through causal attention. A residual interest summary can therefore test persistent preferences without replacing the backbone [1]. (2) Users report broadly related recommendations and excessive influence from occasional purchases. Repeated recent evidence offers a training-derived signal for narrower preferences, although it cannot establish equipment ownership. (3) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin. These identify weak separation, but training margins do not establish validation performance.

**Insights from related work.** (1) MISER separates multiple interests and temporal changes [2]. This motivates distinguishing persistent evidence from recent context, without requiring its full architecture. (2) eSASRec motivates testing sampled softmax [3]. Its combined architectural results do not isolate the objective’s contribution. (3) R2NS motivates delaying hard negatives [4]. Initially using uniform negatives avoids introducing curriculum complexity before establishing a stronger baseline.

**Framework and directions.** Organize interventions along three axes: evidence aggregation, ranking supervision, and content grounding. SASRec supplies ordered aggregation; recurrence pooling adds persistent evidence; multiple negatives strengthen supervision; title encoders potentially add grounding. Compatibility and satisfied needs remain unobserved, so none should become fabricated labels.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Recurrence-gated residual SASRec with uniform multi-negative softmax: 5/7/8/8/4.** Originality: useful combination, established ingredients. Potential: reusable evidence gate, uncertain persistence assumptions. User alignment: targets broad matches and isolated-purchase dominance, cannot verify compatibility. Model alignment: directly tests weak separation, may create false negatives. Difficulty: small additions, requires predictor parity.
- **Scratch-trained title residual: 4/6/7/5/5.** Originality: simple feature fusion, familiar design. Potential: content grounding, sparse text supervision. User alignment: narrower terminology, superficial overlap remains. Model alignment: may separate confusing items, unproven. Difficulty: modest encoder, additional vocabulary artifacts.
- **Warm-started moderate-hard negatives: 4/7/4/9/5.** Originality: known curriculum, task-specific adaptation. Potential: difficult rankings, sampling sensitivity. User alignment: indirect relevance benefits, no explicit preference evidence. Model alignment: targets margin tails, false-negative risk. Difficulty: manageable sampling, extra scoring cost [4].

**Selected algorithm.** Add a bounded residual containing a recency-weighted history summary. Increase history-item weights when their learned embeddings have support from distinct earlier interactions; learn a gate between this summary and SASRec. Train with uniform multi-negative softmax, masking known training positives from negatives. This explicitly targets broad relevance and isolated-purchase dominance, while its objective targets weak positive–negative separation.

Ablate baseline, loss-only, residual-only, and combined variants. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, splits, the 200-epoch environment default, and diagnosis/predictor contracts; charge every run against the shared budget.

idea.description: Recurrence-gated residual SASRec with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax. Preserve the causal SASRec backbone and add a small, bounded summary of recent history weighted by repeated support. Evaluate the representation and objective separately before selecting their combination.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broadly related recommendations and excessive influence from occasional purchases as distinct failures. A recurrence-supported residual explicitly emphasizes sustained recent interests over isolated evidence. Electronics also exhibits weak lower-tail training margins; multiple-negative supervision tests whether stronger discrimination improves held-out ranking. Neither intervention establishes ownership, compatibility, complementarity, or a satisfied need.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only training histories for support computation and negative exclusions. For each causal prefix, normalize its item embeddings and compute similarities against earlier positions; mask padding, self-pairs, and future positions. Define support using the mean of the top few earlier similarities, with zero support when none exist. This is a learned similarity heuristic, not a semantic or compatibility label. Compute pooling weights from a learned nonnegative support coefficient and a learned nonnegative positional-recency penalty. Add a projected pooled vector through a sigmoid gate capped at 0.5; initialize the gate near zero to preserve the starting behavior. Use 32 uniform negatives per supervised position initially; exclude padding, the target, and the user's observed training positives, sampling with replacement when necessary. Chunk supervised positions to bound memory. Use identical scoring in training, validation, prediction, and diagnostics; report raw-logit margins because softmax changes their scale. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must reference the trained module; view.log2feats and view.predict_score must include the residual and scoring path. Omit category breakdowns when category metadata is unavailable, explicitly marking them unavailable. The predictor writer must serialize the architecture configuration and generate working/predict.py with the same model definition and category routing. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Use unchanged pinned validation and no test access. Start with equal-budget baseline and loss-only runs, then test residual-only and combined variants if budget permits; do not assume the combined variant wins.
idea.pseudocode:
For every category, retain the baseline data mapping and splits.
For each batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    h = sasrec_backbone(sequence)
    e = normalize(item_embeddings(sequence))
    similarity[t, j] = dot(e[t], e[j]) for valid j < t
    support[t] = mean(top_k(similarity[t, :t])) or 0
    weights[t, j] = masked_softmax(a * support[j] - b * (t-j)), j <= t
    persistent[t] = sum_j weights[t, j] * item_embeddings(sequence[j])
    gate[t] = 0.5 * sigmoid(gate_network(concat(h[t], persistent[t])))
    features[t] = h[t] + gate[t] * projection(persistent[t])
    negatives = sample_uniform_valid_items(K=32, excluding known training positives)
    logits = shared_score(features, concat(positive, negatives)) / temperature
    loss = cross_entropy(logits[valid_positions], target_column=0)
    optimize(loss)

Run the unchanged pinned validation evaluator.
Compare baseline, loss-only, residual-only, and combined configurations by macro HR@10.
Export the selected checkpoint, configuration, and matching predictor implementation.
Run diagnosis through the same feature and scoring methods.

originality.positive: Combines recurrence-supported residual aggregation with an independently ablated ranking objective under a constrained SASRec interface.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, learned gates, and multi-negative softmax are established techniques; novelty is primarily their targeted integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact basis for later testing temporal recurrence and locally trained content evidence.
future_potential.negative: Repeated interaction similarity may reflect broad popularity or redundant purchases rather than persistent intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small residual module and objective change while retaining the backbone and dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal support computation, negative masking, checkpoint compatibility, and predictor parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to aggregate item histories for sequential recommendation.
Provides the starting backbone and shared item scoring interface.
limitations: The supplied diagnosis suggests that this trained baseline inadequately distinguishes some confusing candidates.
Attention weights alone do not establish compatibility, ownership, or whether a need is satisfied.

related_work.title: MISER
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multiple-interest modeling, temporal changes, and contrastive interest separation.
Motivates separating persistent evidence from recent context.
limitations: Does not establish improvements for this exact benchmark or proposed residual.
Multiple interests alone do not identify expired or satisfied needs.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: The supplied search summary reports a competitive combination of sequential supervision, LiGR layers, and sampled softmax.
limitations: Combined results do not isolate sampled softmax's contribution.
Benefits under the pinned RecHarness protocol remain untested.

related_work.title: R2NS
contributions: The supplied search summary describes uniform warm-start followed by candidate recall and curriculum re-ranking.
limitations: Hard negatives introduce additional scoring cost and false-negative risk.
The proposed first-stage experiment uses uniform negatives and does not reproduce the complete method.
